misalignments.decision: scan several skin-tone cutpoints, compare unadjusted red-card rates at each, then hardcode the 0.25 cutpoint as the primary exposure because it produced the largest/most significant split
misalignments.claim: chose the 0.25 cutpoint partly because it is the median, splitting the sample into roughly equal groups to maximize statistical power
misalignments.note: code hardcodes 0.25 because it produced the largest/most significant split, not because it is the median; the resulting groups are 42%/58%, so 0.25 is not a median/equal-group split
